visual_grammar.background: warm off-white paper base with a subtle low-budget TV-studio grain overlay, plus occasional split-screen fields of muted olive-green and dark charcoal blocks used to stage problem-versus-solution contrast; no glossy gradients
visual_grammar.foreground: near-black text and linework with occasional reversed white text on dark blocks for headline impact
visual_grammar.accent: bright knitted-yarn red matching the mitten color, used sparingly for product highlights, callout boxes, arrows, and key price moments
visual_grammar.typography: bold condensed serif headlines in uppercase for problem/solution statements, paired with plain grotesk sans-serif body text and labels; short direct-response phrases, mixed with occasional italic subheads; all labels tightly kerned and retail-poster-like
visual_grammar.diagram_style: simple retail-infomercial explainer graphics with flat icon silhouettes, split panels, chunky arrows, stamped burst shapes, and minimal charting; no technical UI styling
visual_grammar.panel_style: cream or pale gray rectangular cards with thin charcoal borders, slight inset shadow, and occasional red caption ribbons; feels like hand-composed local advertising rather than corporate SaaS
visual_grammar.grid_system: 12-column poster grid with generous outer margins, strong left alignment, oversized top headline band, and asymmetrical image-text splits that privilege one dominant visual plus 2 to 4 supporting callouts
visual_grammar.line_weight: medium-weight 2 to 3 px divider and outline treatment, with heavier 4 px emphasis rules for before/after splits and price callouts

storyboard.title: Kitten Mittons
storyboard.purpose: Hero cover slide establishing the unforgettable product name, the core promise of quieter, less destructive cats, and the product's visual identity in a single memorable frame. Speaker notes should let Charlie's voice carry the opening while the slide stays clean and sellable.
storyboard.image_prompt: Create a clean full-bleed digital screenshot of a single presentation slide, edge-to-edge, no software UI, no browser chrome, no speaker notes, no page number, no slide count, and no pagination indicator anywhere. This is the one and only title cover slide. Use one dominant hero visual: an illustrative mockup based on the provided source scene showing a gray cat mid-stride wearing four bright red knitted paw mittens on a wooden tabletop, with the quirky home-demo energy preserved but composed more cleanly for a pitch cover. Keep the crouched presenter only as a subtle background figure, secondary to the cat. Large dominant product name at upper left: “KITTEN MITTONS”. One short tagline beneath it: “Quiet paws. Safer furniture.” No other argument text, no charts, no diagrams, no multi-panel layout. Leave generous negative space around the title and hero image so the slide feels like a real exported cover slide.

storyboard.title: The Household Annoyance Is Instantly Legible
storyboard.purpose: Open the argument with the pain, not the joke: noisy paw impacts and clawed furniture. This slide must make the problem feel familiar and retail-urgent for small business investors in seconds.

Right half: concise text framing the problem. Large headline across the top: “CATS SCRATCH. CATS STOMP. storyboard.title: A Visible Fix You Can Understand in One Look
storyboard.purpose: Introduce the product as the oddly sensible answer: elegant, comfortable mittens for cats. The slide should preserve the humor while making the item feel physically real and shelf-ready.

Use an asymmetrical layout with one large hero product mockup on the left: proposed packaged four-mitten retail card showing bright red knitted cat mittens/booties with a die-cut window, bold KITTEN MITTONS wordmark, a small badge reading '1 SIZE FITS ALL', and a simple 3-step illustrated use panel. Add one modest caption ribbon: “Proposed retail pack design.” Do not imply laboratory validation, veterinary approval, or proven performance claims.

storyboard.title: Why This Sells at the Counter
storyboard.purpose: Translate the memorable idea into merchant logic: impulse-buy clarity, fast explanation at shelf, and local-origin credibility. This is where the joke becomes reorder logic.

storyboard.title: What Makes It Investable
storyboard.purpose: Show disciplined upside without pretending scale is already proven: one strong SKU can lead a broader pet-accessory line if demand continues. This slide should reassure investors that the founders understand sequencing.
